status: Repository state on branch feat/release-1652; not deployed.
process: An analyst proposal of 18 editions was checked by two adversarial reviews: one for wrongly included editions, one for wrongly excluded ones. Every number below was re-measured on the verified FULL parquet with duckdb 1.4.4.

Producer statements (README, MANIFEST notes, sources.parquet notes) are claims; ID-CONTRACT.md and FEATURE-FIELD-NOTES.md still name the 1107 freeze and were not relied on. The canonical ID contract, labels and all nine timings were verified at runtime (release-contract.json).
Screens (a)-(c) were applied to all 287 editions with fixed thresholds (edition-screen.csv); none uses edition size.

screens.a_residue: Under 5% of an edition's recorded finishes pass the timing checks. Result: Paris 2014-2018 only (0.03-1.26%; 25 km blank for 97.5-99.6% of finishers after the in-place rewrite).
screens.b_outcome_selective: At least 75% of the fastest finish-time quartile but under 50% of the slowest passes the timing checks. Result: Gold Coast 2024 (95.1/1.4), Barcelona 2019 (79.7/17.8), Dubai 2025 (99.6/41.4), Auckland 2018 (97.1/0.0), Eindhoven 2026 (83.3/9.2). Next: Washington 2017 at 91.4/55.6, kept with a note.
screens.c_mixed_timing_basis: At least 25% of complete nine-checkpoint grids finish at or before 40 km or run 40-42.195 km faster than 2:00/km (gun-time checkpoints with a chip finish). Result: Eindhoven 2026 (65.9%), Barcelona 2019 (50.0%), New York 2007 (40.0%), plus the Paris residue. Next: Warsaw 2025 at 12.4%, kept with a note; New York 2006 6.6%.

released.why: The 0934 hold described a 6,512-record partial load. The edition is now 40,554 records (18,524 women, 22,030 men); both finish-order lists run to their slowest finishers (women 9:02:37, men 9:47:56) with no gaps (largest 3-5 h gap between consecutive finishers 25 s women, 5 s men, the same as accepted Chicago years); no duplicate name+sex+finish groups; 31 records above Running USA's 40,523 finishers. It was reloaded in the same October campaign as the accepted Chicago 2018 and 2019, whose sources rows are equally stale. The producer's freeze notes and the owner's release message name only Chicago 2015 as partial.

kept_held.why: Unchanged since the reviewed 0934 hold (38,047 records, same September 11 sources row); outside totals conflict (NYRR 38,096; Wikipedia and MarathonGuide 37,790), so the 0934 reason, which cites no percentage, is carried. One owner or producer confirmation would release it (37,387 finishes).

Recategorised from invalid_split_grid to unreconciled_hold. The 0934 rows were the 2025 race filed under 2019 (10,373 of their nine-time tuples match Frankfurt 2025) and were deleted; the 10,554 replacements are the real race (winners Fikre Bekele Tefera 2:07:08 and Jemeli Aiyabei 2:19:10; producer note: listed=jsonl=GET=10,554, complete, stamped). Their grids are clean (section shape within about one point of Frankfurt 2018 and 2023-2025), but the producer's feature engine still sets valid_splits false on every row in this freeze. Two producer signals disagree, so the edition is held (10,484 finishes) until the producer confirms the engine constant is stale.

considered_and_kept_with_a_note: Warsaw 2019 and 2022-2025: gun-time checkpoints with a chip finish (producer notes say 'gun'); Warsaw 2025 loses 12% to the timing checks (98.3/78.5 by quartile, screen (b) not met; 12.4% mixed basis, screen (c) not met). The 5-20 km baseline is unaffected; the opening (0-5 km) and last section are biased in every row. Ask the producer for chip splits.

Warsaw 2015-2018 are the spring Orlen race (relabelled in place on 23,919 rows); 2019-2026 the autumn PZU race, whose course profile is supplied as valid from 2019. Runner context now attaches the route only from 2019.

Washington 2017, Dubai 2016 and 2024, Oslo 2017: slow tails cut off by 5-10% (late mats closed early). Helsinki 2017: a 40 km mat gap mid-field. Madrid 2013, 2014, 2022, 2023: mat holes mid-field or an early 25 km mat. All below the screen thresholds.

Chicago 2024: 35 wheelchair results (1:30-2:01, 5 km in 10-13 min) pass the timing bounds. Row-level; the policy is edition-level, so they remain (open item). 3,200 Chicago 2024 rows have no recorded gender; they stay in All and sex is never inferred.

Stockholm 2025, Chicago 2022, 2023 and 2026, Boston 2014, 2015 and 2021, Berlin 2026, Frankfurt 2018 and 2023-2025, Vienna 2023 and 2024, Eindhoven 2025, Warsaw 2020, 2021 and 2026: every finish-time quartile at least about 95% eligible, no sex skew, loads ran to their slowest finishers.

Chicago 2018 and 2019: the 0934 copies of the 2024 field were deleted (all 51,967 and 51,807 IDs) and replaced by 44,550 and 45,864 new records (organiser totals 44,571 and 45,956). No same-city pair among 287 editions shares more than one nine-time tuple, so the stories' duplicate-edition screen is retired.
Valencia 2022-2024: 15,702 rows changed from no recorded gender to F, each with a recorded F- category label (F-SENIOR, F-W45 ...); names, ages and ingested_at unchanged. Not inferred from names.
Cologne 2026 and Prague 2025 (no 20 km split), Honolulu 2021-2025 (no 15-25 km splits): no rule needed, 0 timing-eligible; records stay searchable.
historical_findings: The 0934 cohort included a partial Chicago 2015 (22,085 rows, 22,055 timing-eligible, women to 5:07:55 and men to 4:27:31) that its policy did not hold.

The 0934 cohort also included the editions screens (a)-(c) and the broken loads now exclude (Amsterdam 2020 and 2023, Melbourne 2015, Gold Coast 2024, Auckland 2018, Dubai 2025, Barcelona 2019, New York 2007); EDITIONS.json shows them unchanged since 0934. The 0934 numbers stay as published historical evidence.

New York 2008: a completion stamp (listed = jsonl = GET) would release 37,387 finishes.
Timing basis of the 5 km and later checkpoints versus the finish in Eindhoven 2026, Warsaw 2019-2025, Barcelona 2019 and New York 2007 (gun or chip).
Tokyo 2026: the note promises 1,000 rows (500 per sex); the data hold 770 men.
Paris 2014-2018: why is 25 km blank for about 99% of rows after the in-place rewrite of 203,026 rows' 10-40 km strings (not in CHANGE-REPORT.md)?
Melbourne 2015: about 500 of some 6,000 finishers, with 24 runners loaded two or three times under name variants; no course profile.
Amsterdam 2023: finish loaded for 17 of 16,030 rows.
Chicago 2015: complete the load (about 37,182 finishers reported).
Gold Coast 2024 35 km, Auckland 2018 and Dubai 2025 40 km: are the missing late readings in the source, or in the ingestion?

ID-CONTRACT.md and FEATURE-FIELD-NOTES.md still name the 1107 freeze; the README still carries the old private wording; CHANGE-REPORT.md omits the 116,287 replaced IDs and the 242,649 records changed in place.
